title: Vertical height-one symbolic powers descend through henselian completion
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent Noetherian henselian local normal domain [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $\widehat A$ be its maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and assume $\widehat A$ is a normal domain. Let $0\ne a\in\mathfrak m$. Every prime $P\subseteq\widehat A$ minimal over $a\widehat A$ is of the form $P=\mathfrak p\widehat A$ for a unique prime $\mathfrak p$ minimal over $aA$, namely $\mathfrak p=P\cap A$. For every integer $n\geq1$ one has
$$\mathfrak p^{(n)}\widehat A=P^{(n)}.$$
A prime minimal over an ideal contains that ideal and contains no strictly smaller prime containing it. Both $P$ and $\mathfrak p$ have height one, meaning that they are nonzero and have no prime strictly between zero and themselves. The notation $\mathfrak q^{(n)}$ for a prime of a domain $F$ means $\{x\in F:x/1\in\mathfrak q^n F_{\mathfrak q}\}$, using localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: V 2.2.4 and 3.2.4, pp.65,67: apply minimal-prime descent to A/aA. Symbolic-power comparison: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 0BC0, lemma-symbolic-power-flat-extension (lines 15578--15615).

proof.text: Write $c:A\to\widehat A$ for completion. By faithful flatness of local completion, $c$ is flat; by faithfully flat ideal contraction it is injective and $c^{-1}(J\widehat A)=J$ for every ideal $J\subseteq A$. The completion is Noetherian by the Noetherian completion theorem. Fix a prime $P$ minimal over $c(a)\widehat A$, and set $\mathfrak p=c^{-1}(P)$. Preimages preserve primality, and $a\in\mathfrak p$ since $c(a)\in P$.

The prime $\mathfrak p$ is minimal over $aA$. Indeed, suppose a prime $\mathfrak r\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ contains $a$. Flat going down applied to $A\to\widehat A$, $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p$, and $P$ gives a prime $Q\subseteq P$ contracting to $\mathfrak r$. As $a\in\mathfrak r$, one has $c(a)\in Q$. Minimality of $P$ forces $Q=P$, contradicting their different contractions.

source.place: Tag 00HS, lemma-flat-going-down, applied to the quotient-minimal-prime reduction in ILO V Lemma 2.2.4.

proof.text: Put $B=A/\mathfrak p$. It is a nonzero local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$: primality gives the domain assertion, and primes maximal in the quotient correspond to maximal ideals of $A$ containing $\mathfrak p$. It is Noetherian because its ideals correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $\mathfrak p$. It is excellent by finite-type stability of excellence, since the quotient map makes it an $A$-algebra generated by the empty set. It is henselian by the quotient-henselian-pair theorem, applied with $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Consequently the henselian excellent domain completion theorem says $\widehat B$ is an integral domain. The local quotient-completion theorem, for $A\twoheadrightarrow B$, identifies $\widehat A/\mathfrak p\widehat A\cong\widehat B$. Hence $\mathfrak p\widehat A$ is a proper prime ideal.

source.place: V Lemma 2.2.4, printed p.65, restriction to a generic closure; I Corollary 6.3(ii), printed p.14. Supporting quotient results: Stacks 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent), 09XK (lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair), 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor).

proof.text: By extension, $a\in\mathfrak p$ implies $c(a)\widehat A\subseteq\mathfrak p\widehat A\subseteq P$. Step 3 makes the middle ideal prime, so minimality of $P$ forces $P=\mathfrak p\widehat A$. If another prime $\mathfrak p_0$ minimal over $aA$ has $\mathfrak p_0\widehat A=P$, contraction as established in step 1 gives $\mathfrak p_0=c^{-1}(P)=\mathfrak p$. Thus the descending prime is unique.

source.place: V Lemma 2.2.4, printed p.65, and its use in V 3.2.4, printed p.67; extension/contraction assembly.

proof.text: Apply the principal ideal height bound first in $A$ to $\mathfrak p$ (step 2), and then in the Noetherian ring $\widehat A$ to $P$. Both have height at most one. The element $a$ is nonzero and belongs to $\mathfrak p$, and $c(a)\ne0$ by injectivity in step 1 and belongs to $P$. Thus both primes are nonzero. Since each ambient ring is a domain, zero is prime; a nonzero prime strictly between zero and either prime would produce a prime chain of length two, contradicting the height bound. This is the stated height-one assertion.

source.place: Tag 00KV, lemma-minimal-over-1 (1), lines 14634--14639; height-one use in ILO V 3.2.3(i), printed p.67.

proof.text: For every integer $n\geq1$, apply symbolic powers under flat prime extension to $R=A$, $S=\widehat A$, the flat map $c$ from step 1, and the prime $\mathfrak p$ whose extended ideal is the prime $P$ by step 4. Both rings are Noetherian by the hypotheses and step 1. Its symbolic powers are defined by the same localization membership as in the statement. It gives $\mathfrak p^{(n)}\widehat A=(\mathfrak p\widehat A)^{(n)}=P^{(n)}$, as required.
